In the biblical context, it evokes the idea of inclusion and the opening of divine grace to all peoples, emphasizing that God is not limited to one group. This reflects the theological scope of the universality of salvation, where even those outside the covenant can turn to God and be answered.

This word means 'heavens' and refers to the divine dwelling. In the Bible, the heavens are often associated with God's majesty and sovereignty, where He reigns and hears the prayers of men. Spiritually, this reminds us that God is transcendent and omnipresent, able to respond to the supplications of all, whether they are Israelites or foreigners.

This verb means 'to know' and implies an intimate and relational knowledge. In this verse, it is used to express the desire that all peoples recognize and know the name of God. This underscores the importance of divine revelation and the personal relationship that each individual can have with the Creator, reinforcing the idea that the knowledge of God is essential for fear and worship.

This term means 'house' or 'dwelling,' and in the context of this verse, it refers to the temple built by Solomon. The mishkan is a symbol of God's presence among His people. Theologically, this represents the idea that God desires to dwell in the midst of His people and that the temple is a place where prayers and requests can be presented, reinforcing the idea of communion between God and humanity.

33.epoque: This passage is situated during Solomon's reign, in the 10th century B.C., a period of prosperity and unity for Israel, marked by the construction of the temple in Jerusalem.
33.passage: 2 Chronicles 6 recounts the dedication of the temple by Solomon, where he implores God to listen to the prayers made in this place. This chapter emphasizes the importance of the temple as a meeting point between God and His people.
33.culture: In Israeli culture, the temple was not only a place of worship but also a symbol of the covenant between God and Israel. It represented the divine presence and the centrality of faith in daily life.
33.interpretation: This verse highlights God's openness to all peoples, inviting even foreigners to pray and receive answers. It emphasizes that the knowledge of God and the fear that arises from it should extend beyond Israel, generating a universal testimony.
33.commentaire: This passage reminds us that prayer is accessible to all, regardless of their origin. As Christians, we are called to pray for the nations and to testify of God's love, so that all may know His name and call upon Him. This encourages us to be instruments of peace and reconciliation in our world, sharing the good news of the Gospel.

mots.sens: This term refers to 'people', often in reference to the people of Israel. It evokes the idea of a community united by a covenant with God. In this verse, it emphasizes the collective identity of the Israelites, called to follow God's ways and to address prayers to Him, highlighting their spiritual dependence on Him.

This word means 'enemy' and refers to those who oppose Israel. In the biblical context, enemies can be physical or spiritual adversaries. The mention of enemies here reminds us that God's people are in constant struggle, but they can seek refuge and help in God during these battles.

This term translates to 'prayer' and implies an act of communication with God. Prayer is a means by which the people express their dependence and need for divine help. In this verse, prayer is presented as an essential response of the people in the face of challenges, emphasizing the intimate relationship between God and His people.

This word means 'house' and, in this context, refers to the temple built by Solomon. It represents the place of God's presence among His people. Spiritually, this underscores the importance of a place dedicated to meeting with God, where prayers can be offered and heard.

34.epoque: This verse is set during the reign of Solomon, at a time when Israel was unified and prosperous under God's law, after the construction of the temple in Jerusalem.
34.passage: In 2 Chronicles 6, Solomon dedicates the temple and prays for God to hear the supplications of His people. This chapter emphasizes the importance of God's house as a meeting place between heaven and earth.
34.culture: In Israelite culture, collective prayer and worship at the temple were central. The temple was seen as the place where God's presence resided, and prayers directed towards it were considered powerful and significant.
34.interpretation: This verse teaches that in times of conflict and struggle, God's people must turn to Him in prayer. It highlights the importance of spiritual dependence and seeking divine guidance in trials.
34.commentaire: This passage reminds us that in the face of life's challenges, it is essential to turn to God in prayer. As believers, we should seek to build our spiritual lives around our relationship with God, relying on His promise to hear our supplications. This encourages us to pray not only for our own struggles but also for the faith community, knowing that God is our refuge and strength.

mots.sens: This word means 'heavens' and refers not only to the physical space above us but also to the dwelling place of God. In this context, it evokes divine sovereignty and God's ability to hear and respond to prayers. The notion of heavens also underscores God's transcendence, who is above creation and capable of intervening in human affairs.

This term refers to 'prayer' and implies a personal and direct communication with God. It is often associated with a humble and sincere supplication, where the believer seeks to establish a relationship with the Creator. In the context of this verse, prayer is a means by which the faithful express their dependence on God and their need for justice.

This word means 'to do right' or 'to strengthen' and implies the idea of supporting or defending. In the context of this verse, it suggests that God is the one who brings justice and defends the oppressed. This highlights God's just and fair nature, who responds to the needs of His people by providing comfort and justice.

35.epoque: This passage is set during the reign of Solomon, when the temple in Jerusalem is dedicated, marking a key moment in Israel's history where God's presence is manifested among His people.
35.passage: In this chapter, Solomon dedicates the temple and prays for God to hear the prayers of His people. This verse is part of that prayer, emphasizing the importance of communication between God and Israel and the hope for a divine response.
35.culture: In Israelite culture, prayer was a communal and individual act, essential for maintaining a relationship with God. The temple was the central place for this interaction, where prayers and offerings were presented to God.
35.interpretation: This verse reminds us that God is attentive to the prayers of His people and that He is capable of responding to their needs. It also emphasizes the community's responsibility to turn to God in supplication, seeking His justice and intervention in times of distress.
35.commentaire: This passage invites us to recognize the power of prayer and God's faithfulness in answering the supplications of His people. As believers, we must approach God with confidence, knowing that He hears our cries and acts according to His justice. This encourages us to pray fervently for our needs and those of others, reminding us that our God is a just and merciful God.

mots.sens: This term refers to sin, a deviation from the divine standard. It implies a transgression of God's law, and its roots evoke the idea of missing the mark. Theologically, sin is what separates man from God, and this verse emphasizes that all men are subject to this condition, establishing the necessity of repentance and divine grace.

This word means 'enemy' and refers to those who oppose an individual or a group. In the biblical context, it can also refer to spiritual forces that oppose God's work. The mention of enemies in this verse reminds us that sin can lead to serious consequences, including oppression and captivity, thus highlighting the importance of remaining in communion with God.

This term translates to 'captivity' and evokes the idea of being taken far from one's homeland or freedom. In the biblical context, captivity is often the result of divine judgment for sin. Spiritually, this symbolizes separation from God and the consequences of sin in the lives of believers, highlighting the necessity of reconciliation.

36.epoque: This passage is set during the time of King Solomon, at the dedication of the temple in Jerusalem, a key moment in Israel's history where God's presence is manifested among His people.
36.passage: In this chapter, Solomon addresses a prayer to God, acknowledging human weaknesses and asking for divine mercy for the people of Israel in case of sin. This verse reminds us that even in disobedience, there is a way back to God.
36.culture: At this time, the notion of sin and judgment was deeply rooted in Israelite culture, where obedience to God's law was essential for national prosperity. Captivity was seen as a direct consequence of unfaithfulness to God.
36.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of sin and the reality of divine anger in the face of disobedience. However, it also opens the door to repentance and restoration, reminding us that even in discipline, God remains a God of grace.
36.commentaire: This passage teaches us that sin is a reality for all, but it does not condemn us to a hopeless end. On the contrary, it calls us to repentance and reconciliation with God. As believers, we must recognize our need for God's grace and seek to live in accordance with His will, knowing that He is always ready to welcome those who return to Him.

mots.sens: This word means 'to return' or 'to turn back.' It evokes the idea of repentance and returning to God after a period of distance. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the importance of returning to God to obtain forgiveness and restoration, which is a central theme of biblical faith.

This term means 'to sin' or 'to commit a fault.' It implies an action that deviates from God's will. In this passage, the acknowledgment of sin is essential for the process of repentance and reconciliation with God, highlighting the necessity of sincere confession to receive divine grace.

This word means 'return' or 'repentance.' It is often used to describe the process of returning to God after having sinned. 'Teshuvah' is an act of faith that involves an awareness of one's mistakes and a deep desire to restore the relationship with the Creator, which is fundamental in both Jewish and Christian spirituality.

37.epoque: This passage is set in the context of Solomon's reign, at the time when the Temple in Jerusalem is dedicated, marking a period of prosperity and devotion to God in Israel.
37.passage: In 2 Chronicles 6, Solomon addresses God during the consecration of the Temple, praying for God to hear the supplications of His people, especially in cases of exile or captivity. This verse emphasizes the condition of repentance necessary for God to respond to prayers.
37.culture: At that time, exile was seen as a direct consequence of sin, and returning to the land was often associated with spiritual restoration. The confession of sins was an essential practice in Israelite culture, allowing for the maintenance of a healthy relationship with God.
37.interpretation: This verse teaches that even in captivity, the people have the opportunity to return to God through repentance. It emphasizes that the confession of sins is a crucial step to receive forgiveness and divine restoration, and that God is always ready to listen to those who turn to Him with a sincere heart.
37.commentaire: This passage reminds us of the importance of repentance in our walk with God. No matter the situation we find ourselves in, we always have the opportunity to return to Him, confess our faults, and seek His forgiveness. It encourages us to never lose hope, for God is faithful and desires to restore those who turn to Him with a contrite heart.

mots.sens: This word means 'heart' and represents the center of emotions, will, and thought. In Hebrew culture, the heart is often considered the seat of loyalty and spiritual commitment. In this verse, it underscores the importance of a sincere return to God, involving not only outward actions but a profound inner transformation.

Translated as 'heavens,' this term denotes not only the physical sky but also the presence of God. In the context of prayer, it evokes the idea that prayers ascend to God, who is above all. This reminds believers that God is accessible and attentive to the supplications of His people, even in difficult situations.

This word means 'prayer' and implies direct communication with God. Prayer is an act of submission and dependence on the Creator, and in this verse, it is presented as a means to restore the relationship with God after a period of captivity. This highlights the importance of prayer as a means of repentance and spiritual restoration.

This term is often translated as 'peace,' but it also encompasses notions of well-being, harmony, and wholeness. In the context of this verse, it evokes the desire for reconciliation and restoration between God and His people. It reminds us that returning to God is the path to true peace, both inwardly and outwardly.

38.epoque: This verse is set in the context of Solomon's reign, during the inauguration of the Temple in Jerusalem, a period marked by prosperity and devotion to God.
38.passage: In this chapter, Solomon dedicates the Temple, a place of meeting between God and His people. This verse emphasizes the importance of repentance and prayer, even in times of distress, promising that God will listen to those who turn to Him.
38.culture: In Israelite culture, the Temple was the center of spiritual and communal life. Prayers directed toward the Temple symbolized the desire to restore the relationship with God and return to the promised land.
38.interpretation: This verse emphasizes that returning to God requires an authentic act of repentance, involving the whole heart and soul. It reminds us that even in moments of despair, God is always ready to listen and restore those who turn to Him with sincerity.
38.commentaire: This passage encourages us to examine our own spiritual lives and turn to God with a sincere heart. In our moments of spiritual captivity or distress, we have the promise that God hears our prayers. It is essential to cultivate an authentic relationship with Him, for it is through this sincere return that we can experience His peace and restoration.

mots.sens: This word means 'prayer' and comes from the root 'palal,' which means 'to intercede' or 'to judge.' In the context of 2 Chronicles 6:39, it evokes the idea of a fervent supplication addressed to God, highlighting the importance of communication between man and the Creator. Spiritually, this reminds us that prayer is a means by which believers seek to establish an intimate relationship with God, presenting their needs and seeking His forgiveness.

This term means 'forgiveness' and is derived from the root 's-l-ch,' which implies the idea of release or remission. In this verse, it highlights divine mercy and God's ability to erase the faults of His people. Theologically, this sheds light on God's character as merciful and ready to restore those who turn to Him with repentance.

This word means 'to do right' or 'to justify,' and it is related to the idea of rendering justice or acting according to righteousness. In the context of this verse, it implies that God responds to prayers by acting justly toward His people. Spiritually, this reminds us that God is both just and merciful, and that He cares for those who seek to live according to His ways.

39.epoque: This passage is set during Solomon's reign, as he dedicates the temple in Jerusalem, marking a turning point in Israel's history with God's presence among His people.
39.passage: In 2 Chronicles 6, Solomon addresses God during the dedication of the temple, asking God to listen to the prayers of His people when they turn toward this holy place to seek His help and forgiveness.
39.culture: Prayer and sacrifices were at the heart of Israelite religious life, and the temple represented the meeting place between God and His people. The dedication of the temple was a major event that underscored the importance of divine presence in the community.
39.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the necessity of prayer, repentance, and seeking divine justice. It reminds us that God is attentive to the supplications of His people and is ready to grant forgiveness to those who turn to Him with a sincere heart.
39.commentaire: This passage teaches us the importance of prayer in our relationship with God. As believers, we must approach Him with humility, acknowledging our sins and seeking His forgiveness. It also reminds us that God is always ready to listen and respond to our supplications, offering us hope for redemption and restoration.

mots.sens: This term, which designates God, is in the plural but refers to the uniqueness of God in Hebrew monotheism. It evokes divine power, majesty, and authority. In this verse, it emphasizes God's sovereignty over all things and His role as creator and judge, reinforcing the necessity of addressing Him with respect and faith.

This word means 'prayer' and comes from the root that evokes the idea of 'judging' or 'evaluating.' Prayer is thus perceived as an act of communication with God, where one seeks to align their will with that of the Creator. In the context of this verse, it is presented as a means of invoking God's presence and attention to the needs of the faithful.

This term means 'eyes' and symbolizes the ability to see and understand. In the Bible, God's eyes represent His attention and vigilance over humanity. In this verse, the request for God's eyes to be opened underscores the need for divine intervention and attentive listening to the prayers of believers.

This word means 'ear' and represents the ability to listen and respond. It is often used in the context of listening to God's voice and responding to the prayers of men. In this verse, it highlights the importance of divine listening, emphasizing that God is attentive to the supplications of His people.

40.epoque: This passage is set during the time of Solomon, at the dedication of the temple in Jerusalem, a moment of great importance for the people of Israel and their worship.
40.passage: Chapter 6 of 2 Chronicles describes Solomon's dedication prayer, where he asks God to dwell in the temple and to listen to the prayers made in this place. It is a solemn moment that marks the people's commitment to God.
40.culture: In Israelite culture, the temple was considered God's dwelling on earth, a sacred place where prayers were particularly powerful. The dedication of the temple was a communal act that united the people in faith.
40.interpretation: Spiritually, this verse emphasizes the importance of prayer in the lives of believers and their need for a personal relationship with God. It reminds us that God is attentive to the hearts that turn to Him with sincerity.
40.commentaire: This verse teaches us that prayer is a powerful means of communion with God. As believers, we must remember that God is always attentive to our supplications and desires us to come to Him in faith. May our prayer be an expression of our dependence on Him, and may we seek His presence in all our actions.

mots.sens: This term designates God in His creative and sovereign power. As a plural, it emphasizes God's majesty and greatness, while being used in a singular context to express the uniqueness of the Eternal. In this verse, Elohim evokes the divine presence manifested in the temple, symbolizing the connection between God and His people.

This word means 'glory' or 'majesty' and refers to the splendor and dignity of God. It is often associated with the divine presence, particularly in the context of the tabernacle and the temple. In this verse, it underscores the importance of the ark as a symbol of God's presence among His people.

This term designates an offering, often a grain or bread oblation, presented to God. It symbolizes recognition and gratitude towards God for His blessings. In this context, it reminds us of the importance of worship and devotion in the spiritual lives of the priests and the people.

This word means 'peace' but also encompasses notions of well-being, prosperity, and harmony. It is central to the relationship between God and His people, representing the ideal state of communion and security. In this verse, it evokes the happiness that God's beloved can experience in His presence.

41.epoque: This passage is set during the time of Solomon, at the inauguration of the temple in Jerusalem, a key moment in Israel's history where God's presence is manifested in a tangible way.
41.passage: This verse is part of the temple dedication prayer, where Solomon calls on God to establish His presence among His people. It emphasizes the importance of the relationship between God, His priests, and the people of Israel.
41.culture: In Israelite culture, the temple is the place of encounter with God, and sacrifices are expressions of devotion and gratitude. Solomon's prayer reflects a deep understanding of the necessity of divine presence in communal life.
41.interpretation: Spiritually, this verse calls for a renewed communion with God, where the priests are clothed with salvation and the people enjoy peace. It reminds us that God's presence brings security and joy to those who are faithful to Him.
41.commentaire: This passage invites us to seek God's presence in our daily lives. Just as Solomon did, we must pray for God to rise and dwell among us, clothing us with His salvation. As believers, we are called to live in the peace and joy that only God's presence can bring.

mots.sens: This term means 'anointed' and designates one who has been consecrated with oil for a sacred function. In the biblical context, it refers to kings and priests, symbolizing divine authority and God's protection. Spiritually, this evokes the special relationship between God and His people, as well as the messianic expectation, since Jesus is the Messiah, the anointed one of God.

This verb means 'to remember' and implies an action of God who recalls and acts in favor of His promises. In this verse, it emphasizes the importance of God's faithfulness to David and his descendants, affirming that God does not forget His commitments. Theologically, this reminds us that God is a God of promise who acts according to His word.

This term designates God's goodness, grace, or faithfulness towards His people. It evokes a relationship of unconditional love and mercy, often linked to divine covenants. In the context of this verse, it reminds us that the graces granted to David reflect God's faithfulness to those He has chosen.

This word means 'servant' and is often used to designate those called to serve God. In the case of David, it highlights his role as king and leader after God's own heart. Spiritually, this calls us to recognize our own position as servants of God, called to live according to His will.

42.epoque: This verse is set in the context of the Old Testament period, during the reign of Solomon, son of David, as the temple is being built in Jerusalem.
42.passage: In this chapter, Solomon dedicates the temple and offers a prayer to God, asking for His presence and blessing upon this place. Verse 42 is a supplication for God to remember His covenant with David.
42.culture: Israeli culture deeply valued the covenant between God and His people, as well as the monarchy, which was seen as a divine institution. The remembrance of the promises made to David was essential for maintaining the people's hope and faith.
42.interpretation: This verse expresses a supplication for God to remember His promises and faithfulness to David. It underscores the importance of divine memory in the relationship between God and His people, and the hope that the graces granted to David continue in the royal lineage.
42.commentaire: This passage reminds us that God is faithful to His promises and remembers those who are consecrated to Him. As believers, we can rely on God's faithfulness, knowing that He acts according to His promises. This encourages us to live as servants of Christ, confident in His love and grace.
